# Europa.vim — Copilot code-review instructions

## Project context

Europa.vim is a Vim/Neovim plugin for viewing Jupyter notebooks, built on denops.vim with Deno + TypeScript.

The codebase follows a **three-tier Source of Truth**: TypeBox schemas (`schema/`) define data shapes → BDD specs (`tests/spec/`) define behavior → implementation (`denops/europa/`) plus hand-written guide chapters (`doc/sources/`) form the documentation layer. Inferred types and `doc/europa.txt` are derived outputs — never hand-edited.

## Hard rules — flag any violation

### Types and schemas

- Hand-written `interface` or `type` aliases outside `contracts/*.ts` are forbidden. All types must be derived via `Static<typeof Schema>` from TypeBox schemas in `schema/`.
- Do not suggest replacing TypeBox schemas in `schema/**/*.ts` with plain `interface`/`type` — schemas are the Source of Truth, not boilerplate.

### Generated files

- `doc/europa.txt` is generated by `deno task gen:vimdoc` and must never be hand-edited. Flag any direct edits to this file.

### Documentation placement

- Hand-written documentation is allowed only in: `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `DESIGN.ja.md`, `doc/sources/*.txt`. Flag new `.md` or `.txt` files added anywhere else.

### Agent config files

- `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` are symlinks and must not be edited directly. `AGENTS.md` may be modified only when the PR explicitly states it is changing agent instructions.

### Language

- All in-code comments, identifiers, TSDoc, and commit messages must be in English (CONTRIBUTING.md §8). Flag Japanese text in `*.ts` or `*.vim` source files, including inline code-block comments.

### Spec linkage

- BDD spec ↔ TSDoc linkage uses `@spec-id europa.<area>.<topic>` tags exclusively (e.g. `europa.notebook.parse.normalize`). Heading-name-based matching is forbidden — it breaks under renames.
- From Phase 2 onward, public APIs annotated with `@spec-id` require TSDoc with `@param`, `@returns`, `@example`, and `@throws` where applicable.

## Testing & CI

- The full CI gate is `deno task check`: runs `fmt:check → lint → validate → gen:vimdoc → test:fixtures → test:spec → test:golden → git diff --exit-code doc/europa.txt` in sequence. All steps must pass before merging.
- From Phase 2+, any PR adding new runtime behavior must include a BDD spec under `tests/spec/**/*_spec.ts` with a stable `@spec-id`. Flag implementation-only PRs that skip this requirement.
- Golden fixtures under `tests/golden/` must be updated deliberately — never just to silence a failing test.

## Commit & PR conventions

- Commit subject line: emoji prefix (e.g. `:sparkles:`, `:bug:`, `:books:`) + imperative-mood summary + 72 characters max. Body explains the WHY.
- Every PR must declare its phase (`Phase 0`–`Phase 5`) in the description. Mixed-phase PRs should be split.
- From Phase 2+, PR body must list the `@spec-id` values the PR implements.

## What NOT to flag

- TypeBox verbosity in `schema/**/*.ts` — intentional SoT design, not boilerplate to simplify.
- Japanese prose in `DESIGN.ja.md` — it is a synchronized translation of `DESIGN.md` and is intentional.
- Missing TSDoc on private or internal helpers — full TSDoc is required only on `@spec-id`-annotated public APIs.
- The content of `doc/europa.txt` — only flag if there is clear evidence the file was hand-edited rather than regenerated via `deno task gen:vimdoc`.
- Absence of inline comments on self-explanatory code — the project deliberately avoids comments unless the WHY behind a decision is non-obvious.
